None of the candidate papers directly investigate the nature of the accretion process in LS I +61 303 or the relationship between gamma-ray emission and accretion models. They are all adjacent, discussing related phenomena or observations.

They provide substantive new evidence on the variability and propagation of jets, contributing to understanding the discrepancies in durations.
None of the candidate papers directly investigate the specific mechanisms causing different spectral behaviors in magnetars or their relation to re-brightening bumps in GRBs and SGRs.
None of the candidate papers directly investigate the relationship between HFQPO frequency ratios and neutron star spin frequency in the specified microquasars.

None of the candidate papers directly investigate the specific question of the underlying physical mechanisms accounting for the similarity in the flux spectra of 1E 1048.1-5937 and 4U 0142+61, nor do they challenge the dust disk model proposed for 1E 1048.1-5937.

The paper [1401.5000] provides a long-term X-ray flux and spectral analysis of 1RXS J170849.0-400910, finding low-level spectral variations but no significant X-ray flux variations, contributing substantive evidence on part of the question regarding spectral variability and X-ray emission characteristics.

None of the candidate papers directly investigate the discrepancies between inferred and observationally inferred TDE rates or the reconciliation of black hole mass estimates from CIV and Hb line measurements.

However, it does not fully resolve the question, leaving it partially addressed.

Both contribute substantive new evidence on aspects of the question, but do not fully resolve it.

However, it does not fully settle the implications for the proto-magnetar hypothesis.
